name: Northern and Southern Dynasties
summary: A period when China was divided between northern dynasties (led by the Xianbei Northern Wei) and southern dynasties based at Jiankang. Buddhism flourished, with the great cave temples of Yungang and Longmen.

location.value: North China under the Northern Wei and its successors; south China under the Song, Qi, Liang and Chen.
location.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

terrain.value: The northern plain and the Yangtze valley, divided by the Huai river.

resources.value: Northern farmland; southern rice land opened by migrants.

disasters.value: War and famine in the north.

urbanisation.value: Northern Wei moved its capital from Pingcheng to Luoyang in 493; Jiankang was the southern capital.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

disease.value: No major epidemics are recorded in the sources checked.

migration.value: Large-scale migration of Han Chinese south of the Yangtze.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

economicBase.value: The equal-field land system in the north; trade and a money economy in the south.

tradeRoutes.value: Silk Road trade in the north; maritime trade from the south.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: The Northern Wei equal-field system (485) set land and taxes.

inequality.value: Aristocratic families dominated, especially in the south.

governmentType.value: Rival monarchies; Xianbei-ruled states in the north.

keyRulers.value: Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei (471–499), Emperor Wu of Liang (502–549).

succession.value: Frequent coups; southern rulers were often generals.

institutions.value: The equal-field system, later used by the Sui and Tang.

stability.value: Frequent civil war and changes of dynasty.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

eliteConflict.value: The Hou Jing rebellion devastated the Liang (548–552).

armyAndTech.value: Heavy cavalry, helped by the stirrup.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

majorWars.value: Wars between north and south; the Hou Jing rebellion (548–552).

territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

alliancesRivals.value: North versus south; the Rouran on the steppe.

inventions.value: Zu Chongzhi calculated π to seven decimals and made the Daming calendar (465).
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

scienceEducation.value: Advances in medicine, astronomy, mathematics and cartography (Tao Hongjing, Zu Chongzhi).
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

openness.value: Sinicisation of non-Han peoples in the north.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

religion.value: Mahayana Buddhism spread widely, alongside Daoism.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

languageWriting.value: Chinese; Xiaowen’s reforms made Chinese the court language in the north.

sharedIdentity.value: Rival claims to be the true heirs of Chinese civilisation.

neighbours.value: The Rouran, Goguryeo, Baekje and Tuyuhun.

ideasReligions.value: Buddhism became a mass religion with great cave temples.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026); Lewis, China Between Empires (2009)

riseSignals.value: Liu Song founded in 420; Northern Wei unified the north (439).
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

peakPeriod.value: Northern Wei under Xiaowen; Liang under Emperor Wu.

declineSignals.value: Northern Wei split (534); Hou Jing rebellion in the south.

outcome.value: Emperor Wen of Sui reunified China in 589.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

sources.value: Official histories. Checked against Wikipedia (“Northern and Southern dynasties”).
sources.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Dates for some dynasties vary between sources.
overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Northern and Southern dynasties (checked 6 Nov 2026)

knownFor.label: Yungang & Longmen Grottoes
knownFor.note: Huge Buddhist cave temples carved into cliffs.

knownFor.label: Zu Chongzhi’s π
knownFor.note: Calculated π accurately to seven decimal places.
